transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what finally made me ask for help is that I just keep forgetting these little things that I normally handle without an issue. Like, I'll forget to return phone calls, or I'll completely forget to turn in a registration form. Actually, that form was for my niece's baking class, and my sister was so annoyed with me because they almost lost their spot. She always gets like that, though. Even when we were kids, if I forgot to bring her hairbrush back or something, she would just hold a grudge for days. She has this really long, thick curly hair, so I guess I get why she was protective of her stuff, but still. 

Um... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, just forgetting stuff. Like even just telling myself I need to stop for an errand on the way home from work, and then I just completely drive right past the store and go straight home. I don't know, it's just been really bothering me lately.
Have you struggled with this kind of forgetfulness and difficulty staying on top of tasks since you were a child, or is this a relatively new change for you?

Oh, it's definitely not new. Even back in elementary school, I was always that kid who forgot permission slips, or I'd completely lose my homework at the bottom of my backpack. Actually, I had this amazing Lisa Frank backpack in fourth grade—it had those neon tigers on it, you know? I begged my mom for it for literally months because all the girls in my class had them. But then I left a banana in the front pocket over a long weekend and it got totally smushed and ruined the fabric. It smelled so bad for the rest of the year, and my mom was so mad at me because they were kind of expensive. 

But yeah, she... um, she and my teachers always had to remind me step by step to finish any of my school projects. Like if we had a science fair thing, I'd get stuck just decorating the title on the poster board and forget to actually do the rest of it. I'd just get so wrapped up in the glitter and the markers, and then my mom would have to sit at the kitchen table and walk me through every single step just to get it done by morning. 

Wait, did you ask about school or work? I'm sorry, I totally lost my train of thought.
Do you often feel like you have a 'motor' inside you that keeps you constantly active, or do you find it hard to sit still for long periods of time?

Um, I don't know if I'd call it a motor, exactly. Like, I'm not running laps around the office or anything. But I definitely have a hard time just sitting completely still. Like, whenever I have to sit through those really long training classes at work—we actually just had a three-hour one for this new scheduling software—I always notice myself clicking my pen or bouncing my foot the whole time. I'll just be shifting around in my chair constantly, even when I'm really trying to sit perfectly still and pay attention to the presenter. 

Actually, speaking of pens, I was using my absolute favorite one during that training. It's one of those gel ones, but it has to be the ultra-fine point because the medium ones smudge everywhere. Especially on that weird, glossy paper they always use to print the training manuals. My boss always orders the absolute cheapest bulk pens for the supply closet, the ones that barely even write and just scratch the paper, you know? So I started buying my own and hiding them in my bottom desk drawer. But Brenda, the receptionist, she's always coming over and "borrowing" them and I literally never see them again. It drives me crazy because they aren't cheap. So now I have a little lockbox in there... 

Um, wait. Sorry. Did that answer your question? I feel like I totally just started rambling about office supplies. What did you ask me again?
Do you often find yourself acting or speaking without thinking, such as interrupting others during conversations or making impulsive decisions?

Um, not really? I mean, I don't think I'm impulsive or anything. I don't really interrupt people, at least I try not to. I know how annoying that is. My ex-boyfriend used to do that all the time. Like, I'd be right in the middle of telling him about a really stressful phone call I had at work—because dealing with some of our clients is just exhausting, they'll call and complain about literally anything—and he would just cut me off to talk about his fantasy football team. It was so rude! I mean, I don't even understand fantasy football. Why would you spend hours obsessing over stats for players who aren't even on the same real-life team? It just seems like a lot of extra math for no reason. I was never very good at math, honestly. In high school, I had to take algebra twice because the first teacher I had just mumbled into the chalkboard the whole time. 

Oh, sorry, what were we talking about? Did you ask about interrupting people? Yeah, no, I don't really do that. I usually just kind of zone out if I'm not talking, to be honest.
